title: Cocktails on Film
intro: Familiar drinks. Unforgettable scenes. A short guide to cocktails with a place in movie history.
notice: Independent editorial content, not an extension of our beverage menu. Ingredient lists describe common versions, not exact on-screen recipes. Ask the bar about availability.

drinks.name: White Russian
drinks.note: The Dude’s signature order gives this creamy coffee cocktail a central place in the film’s identity.

drinks.name: Vesper
drinks.note: Bond’s gin-and-vodka drink originated in Ian Fleming’s novel before its screen appearance. Modern versions often use Lillet Blanc in place of the original Kina Lillet.
drinks.ingredients: Gin · Vodka · Lillet Blanc · Lemon twist

drinks.name: Dry Martini
drinks.note: Nick and Nora Charles helped make the Martini a screen icon. The Nick & Nora glass takes its name from the fictional detective couple.
drinks.ingredients: Gin · Dry vermouth · Olive or lemon twist

drinks.name: French 75
drinks.note: Ordered at Rick’s Café, this sparkling cocktail belongs to the film’s world of late-night conversations and complicated loyalties.

drinks.name: Champagne Cocktail
drinks.note: The Champagne Cocktail is another classic ordered in the film, pairing sugar and bitters with sparkling wine.
